rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalili explains iftā as giving strength by clarifying a difficult matter.
rows.anchor: “İftâ” bir müşkilin beyânıyla kuvvet vermektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because iftā is a term familiar from religious law, its use suggests the council has a kind of legal authority.
rows.anchor: bu tâbir, bu meclisin şer‘î bir salâhiyetini ifadeden hâlî değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fī amrī can mean either “in my affair” or “about the order I will issue.”
rows.anchor: Emrimde yani bu işimde, yahut vereceğim emir hakkında

words: مَا كُنتُ قَاطِعَةً أَمْرًا حَتَّىٰ تَشْهَدُونِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The queen says she has made no state decision autocratically and has put none into effect without hearing the council; she seeks their advice on this letter too.
rows.anchor: Yani şimdiye kadar devlet umûrundan hiçbirinde istibdad yapmadım, sizin re’yinizi almadan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording implies a council accustomed to assembling before the queen to deliberate on important matters.
rows.anchor: denilmesinden bunların mühim işleri müşavere için huzûrunda toplanması mu‘tad olan bir heyet olduğu anlaşılıyor.

rows.speaker: Katâde
rows.claim: Qatada reports that the council had 312 members, each representing ten thousand people.
rows.anchor: Bunların her biri on bin kişiyi temsil etmek üzere üç yüz on iki kişi olduğu da rivayet edilmiştir (Katâde).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praising the absence of autocracy and the council’s role establishes the importance of consultation, outwardly resembling a constitutional custom.
rows.anchor: bunun zâhiri bir meşrutiyet teâmülü anlatmaktadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The consultation does not extend to intervention in command; it remains lawful counsel and advice, which is why exegetes stress consultation’s importance.
rows.anchor: meşrû bir meşveret ve iftâ mâhiyetinden ileri gitmediği için müfessirîn burada yalnız istişarenin ehemmiyetinden bahsetmişlerdir.

words: نَحْنُ أُو۟لُوا۟ قُوَّةٍۢ وَأُو۟لُوا۟ بَأْسٍۢ شَدِيدٍۢ
rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some read the council’s reply as saying that its members are soldiers, not political advisers, and will do whatever the queen orders.
rows.anchor: Bazıları bu sözü, biz kuvvet adamları, harb u darb ehli askerleriz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although this reading captures a military outlook, the passage’s flow shows the gathering is not merely a military council.
rows.anchor: أَفْتُونِى فِىٓ أَمْرِى diye başlayan kelâmın cereyânı sade bir şûrâyı askerîden ibaret olmamasında zâhirdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We” means the strength of the state and community addressed by the letter, not the individual councillors.
rows.anchor: “Biz” diyenler şahıslarını değil, mektuba muhatab olan cemiyetin, yani devletlerinin kuvvetini kasdetmişlerdir.

words: نَحْنُ أُو۟لُوا۟ قُوَّةٍۢ وَأُو۟لُوا۟ بَأْسٍۢ شَدِيدٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They foresee that resisting surrender may require war, but do not demand war or interfere with the queen’s authority; they defer to her and signal openness to peace.
rows.anchor: emre müdahaleyi tecviz etmiyorlar da harb olmaksızın bir çare bulunabildiği takdirde memnun olacaklarını andırır bir surette

words: إِنَّ ٱلْمُلُوكَ إِذَا دَخَلُوا۟ قَرْيَةً أَفْسَدُوهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The queen argues that invading monarchs devastate a land and humiliate its honored people through killing, captivity, exile, imprisonment, and other calamities.
rows.anchor: Katl, esaret, nefy, hapis vesâire gibi envâ‘-ı zillet ve felâkete giriftar ederler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She includes Solomon among such rulers because he has warned them not to act arrogantly toward him, so she urges avoiding war and conquest.
rows.anchor: أَلَّا تَعْلُوا۟ عَلَىَّ diyen Süleyman da böyle yapar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The queen sends a gift to probe Solomon’s character, see whether he can be appeased with wealth, and decide how to proceed.
rows.anchor: Yani bu suretle huylarını yoklayacağım da ona göre hareket edeceğim. Bakalım mâl ü menâl ile savulabilecek kimseler mi?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the envoy reaches Solomon, Solomon refuses the gift.
rows.anchor: vaktâ ki gönderilen, Süleyman’a vardı hediyeyi kabul etmeyip şu suretle reddetti.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text does not identify this assembly explicitly; Elmalili takes it to be the commanders of Solomon’s troops.
rows.anchor: bu “mele’”den murad îzah edilmemiştir وَحُشِرَ لِسُلَيْمَٰنَ جُنُودُهُۥ مِنَ ٱلْجِنِّ وَٱلْإِنسِ وَٱلطَّيْرِ’deki cünûdun rüesâsı olsa gerektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon knows they are relying on their gift; after returning it with a threatening message, he expects their arrival and plans a marvel that may lead them to faith.
rows.anchor: Süleyman aleyhisselâm onların hediyelerine güvendiklerini bilmiş idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the queen, told of Solomon’s message, recognized he was more than an ordinary king, then came with many leaders to learn his command and religion while securing her throne behind locked doors.
rows.anchor: Rivayet olunur ki elçiler kadına varıp Süleyman aleyhisselâm’ın dediğini anlattıklarında “bilmiş vallahi, bu sade bir melik değil, biz buna tâkat getiremeyiz”

rows.speaker: Râgıb
rows.claim: Raghib’s Mufradat glosses ifrit as fierce and wicked, hence a tough or formidable being.
rows.anchor: Râgıb’ın Müfredât’ında: “‘ifrit’ هو العارم الخبيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ifrit can be used metaphorically for a human, as in the expression “ifrit nifrit.”
rows.anchor: Şeytan gibi insana da istiare olunur, ‘ifrit nifrit’ denilir.

rows.speaker: İbn Kuteybe
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba derives ifrit from a strong constitution; the source also connects its root to wrestling and throwing an opponent down.
rows.anchor: İbn Kuteybe demiştir ki: ‘İfrit, müvesseku’l-halk, yani hilkati kuvvetli demektir.

rows.speaker: Ebû Amr b. Abdülberr
rows.claim: Abu Amr ibn Abd al-Barr transmits a terminology ranking: jinn, cohabiting ʿāmirs, child-afflicting spirits, devils, then stronger and more wicked ifrits.
rows.anchor: Ebû Amr b. Abdülberr’den naklen der ki: “Lisâna âlim olan ehl-i kelâm cinni merâtib üzere zikrederler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ifrit is exceptionally wicked, clever, strong, and hard to manage; because the term can also describe a person, the verse specifies that this one is from the jinn.
rows.anchor: Demek ki “ifrit” şerr ü habâsette dehâ ve şeytanette ileri gitmiş, tuttuğunu devirir, kuvvetli

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Solomon sat in his audience place each day from morning until noon.
rows.anchor: her gün makamında sabahtan öğleye kadar oturur idiği rivayet olunuyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ifrit emphatically assures Solomon that he can bring the throne easily, honestly, unchanged, and without losing anything.
rows.anchor: kolay getiririm, hem de hiçbir hıyanet etmem, tebdîl ü tağyir etmeden hiçbir şey zâyi‘etmeksizin getiririm

rows.speaker: İbn Mes‘ud
rows.claim: Ibn Masud identifies the person with knowledge of the Book as Khidr.
rows.anchor: İbn Mes‘ud kavlince Hızır aleyhisselâm’dır.

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas’s well-known view identifies him as Solomon’s vizier Asaf ibn Barakhya, a truthful man who knew the Greatest Name; his answered prayer was a miracle through Solomon’s vizier.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’ın[^9] meşhur olan kavlince Süleyman aleyhisselâm’ın veziri Âsaf

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Razi prefers Solomon himself: the relative clause should identify a known possessor of book-knowledge, and 27:15–16 already describe Solomon as given knowledge and taught the speech of birds.
rows.anchor: Fahreddin Râzî bu zâtın Süleyman aleyhisselâm’ın kendisi olması kavlini vücûh ile tercih etmiştir. Ezcümle mevsûlün

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the reading that the knowledgeable person is Solomon, he speaks directly to the ifrit.
rows.anchor: ancak bu surette أَنَا۠ ءَاتِيكَ بِهِۦ hitâbı ifritedir. Süleyman ifrite karşı söylemiştir.

rows.speaker: ekseriyet
rows.claim: The majority take the knowledgeable figure to be one of Solomon’s companions, which they consider more consistent with the narrative flow.
rows.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh ekseriyet, bu zâtın Süleyman aleyhisselâm’ın

rows.speaker: Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
rows.claim: Ibn Arabi says the throne was brought through a companion of Solomon so that Solomon’s rank would appear still greater to those present.
rows.anchor: Muhyiddîn-i Arabî Füsûs’ta demiştir ki: “Bu Süleyman aleyhisselâm’ın ashâbından bazısının eliyle oldu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A companion’s extraordinary act reflects even greater honor for Solomon and shows that the companion’s knowledge was bestowed on him.
rows.anchor: Şüphesiz ashâbından böyle kerametin zuhûru kendisinin daha ziyade yüksekliğine delâlet eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prior report in the hoopoe story places the journey at Sanaa; Sanaa is said to be three days from Sheba.
rows.anchor: Yukarıda hüdhüd kıssasında San‘a’ya kadar varıldığına dair bir rivayet geçmişti, San‘a’dan ise Sebe’ üç günlük mesafedir deniliyor.

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Others say Solomon had returned from Sanaa and was in the land of Syria, making the distance two months.
rows.anchor: Bazıları da bu sıra Süleyman aleyhisselâm San‘a’dan dönmüş, Şam arzında bulunuyordu demişler. Bu takdirde iki aylık mesafe demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given the proposed distances, this was not an ordinary event but a miracle or saintly marvel.
rows.anchor: Şüphe yok ki bu alelâde vekâyi‘den değil bir keramet ve mucize olmak üzere mevzû‘-i bahistir.

rows.speaker: Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
rows.claim: Ibn Arabi explains that Asaf annihilated the throne at its location and recreated it beside Solomon; its existence and nonexistence coincided, so it traversed no distance.
rows.anchor: Muhyiddîn-i Arabî bunu şöyle anlatmıştır: “Âsaf, tahtın aynında tasarruf etti de onu mevzi‘inde i‘dam edip

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Arabi derives his doctrine of continual new creation from Qaf 50:15, a theory later carried as far as Descartes.
rows.anchor: Şeyhin بَلْ هُمْ فِى لَبْسٍۢ مِّنْ خَلْقٍۢ جَدِيدٍۢ [Kāf 50/15]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalili rejects applying that theory here: the verse says “I will bring it,” not “I will make it,” and describes a time interval.
rows.anchor: Çünkü “yaparım” denmemiş, “getiririm” denilmiştir. قَبْلَ أَن يَرْتَدَّ إِلَيْكَ طَرْفُكَ denilmesiyle de bir zaman ifade edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means longer than a blink or a glance itself: it spans the eye’s return, which can exceed a second.
rows.anchor: Lemh-i basar değil, tarfetü’l-ayn da değil, bunlardan daha uzun olarak قَبْلَ أَن يَرْتَدَّ إِلَيْكَ طَرْفُكَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Arabi treats the interval as one instant to avoid motion’s apparent contradiction, but motion takes at least two instants; the verse instead denotes the quickest time.
rows.anchor: Lâkin Şeyh bunu bir an telakkī etmiş, hâlbuki hareket mefhûmu lâekal iki an iktizâ eylediği cihetle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The knowledgeable person says he will bring the throne rather than create it; because he already knows how, saying the words and bringing it coincide.
rows.anchor: fiil îcad değil ityandır. Bunu söylemesiyle getirmesi bir olmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Modern scientific thought already accepts speeds of thousands of kilometers per second; the important question is what force can produce such motion, including motion of a mass.
rows.anchor: Bir saniyede binlerce kilometre sür‘at, zamanımız efkâr-ı fenniyesinin mülâhazasına alışmış olduğu mesâildendir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speed seen in a spark, current, or telegraph could also occur in a mass; will can act remotely, and a distant object’s movement by will is knowledge established in the Book and Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: Bir sâ‘ikada, bir cereyanda, bir telgrafta görülen bu sür‘at bir kütlede de görülebilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reported view is that this revelation to Moses’s mother was inspiration or a dream, not prophetic revelation.
rows.anchor: Bu vahyin nübüvvet vahyi değil, ilham veya rüya demek olduğunu söylüyorlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although theologians do not treat inspiration as a general source of knowledge, it can compel action for the person who receives it.
rows.anchor: umum için esbâb-ı ilimden olmamakla beraber

words: إِنَّا رَآدُّوهُ إِلَيْكِ وَجَاعِلُوهُ مِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic promise gives certainty, as does the natural maternal impulse to nurse; this was saintly inspiration, not prophetic revelation.
rows.anchor: teminatı sîga-i tahkik ile kat‘iyyet de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inspiration is understood to have come after Moses’s birth and after he had been nursed for a time; one report says three months.
rows.anchor: Anlaşılıyor ki bu ilham, Mûsâ doğduktan sonra olmuş ve biraz emzirilmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalili identifies al-yamm here as the Nile.
rows.anchor: {فِى ٱلْيَمِّ} Nil {خَٰطِـِٔينَ} “hatâ”dan değil, “hatîe”dendir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khāṭiʾīn derives from khatīʾa, “sin,” rather than khaṭaʾ, “mistake”; the latter would take the form mukhṭiʾīn.
rows.anchor: “hatâ”dan değil, “hatîe”dendir. Çünkü “hatâ”da “muhtiîn” denilir.

words: إِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ وَهَٰمَٰنَ وَجُنُودَهُمَا كَانُوا۟ خَٰطِـِٔينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their being sinners explains why Moses would become their enemy and grief: God afflicted them in this way, and otherwise they would not have taken him in.
rows.anchor: Bu âyet لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوًّۭا وَحَزَنًا hikmetinin vechini beyandır. Yani cânî oldukları için Allah tarafından o suretle mübtelâ olacaklardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mother’s heart was empty because shock and bewilderment left her with no news of Moses and with her mind nearly blank.
rows.anchor: gönlü bomboş sabahı etti bunun zâhiri ne olup kaldığından hiçbir haber almayarak hayretten ve dehşetten gönlüne hiçbir şey girmiyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In her anxious effort to learn what happened, she nearly revealed what she had done and exposed Moses.
rows.anchor: Az daha onu meydana verecekti telâş ile haber alacağım diye yaptığını sezdirecek, Mûsâ’yı ifşâ edecekti.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’s mother told his sister to follow his trail and find out what had happened to him.
rows.anchor: “kardeşinin izini tâkip et” -ne olduğundan bir haber al- demişti.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turkish does not distinguish masculine and feminine pronouns, but the Arabic says “his sister,” Moses’s sister, not his mother’s sister.
rows.anchor: Hâlbuki لاُِخْتِها değil لِأُخْتِهِۦ’dir. Şu hâlde zâhir olan لِبِنْتِهَا “kendi kızına” denilmek iken

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying “his sister” rather than “her daughter” more eloquently emphasizes the sister’s affection for Moses.
rows.anchor: “onun hemşiresine” denilmesi şefkate tansis nokta-i nazarından daha beliğ olmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’s sister watched him from a distance.
rows.anchor: o da onu uzaktan gözledi, gördü

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They” are Pharaoh’s household; they did not notice the watching or realize the watcher was Moses’s sister.
rows.anchor: Gözettiğinin yahut hemşiresi olduğunun farkına varmıyorlardı.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-malaʾ addresses the people, specifically a conspicuous, impressive gathering.
rows.anchor: ey millet: ey şu gözler dolduran cemaat

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalili frames Pharaoh’s address as the act of a tyrant summoning his community.
rows.anchor: Firavun ise -bak ne zâlim, cemiyetini toplayıp da- dedi ki

words: مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh knows he did not create his people and has a creator himself, yet denies God’s exclusive right to divinity and wrongs the concepts of creation and godhood.
rows.anchor: Pekâlâ bilir ki şu halkı yaratan kendisi değildir, kendisini de bir yaratan vardır.

words: مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He presents lawmaking and government as his own will with no higher authority, demanding that people obey, love, fear, and worship him.
rows.anchor: ne irade ederse olurmuş, hükm ü hükûmetini nakzedebilecek mâfevk bir kuvvet yokmuş gibi gösteriyor.

words: مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By saying “I know of no other god” rather than “there is none,” Pharaoh tries to appear fair-minded.
rows.anchor: İlk önce “yoktur” demiyor, “bilmiyorum” diye insaflı görünmek istiyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh insinuates that the Lord of heaven and earth is a physical object that could be seen by surveying the sky, using a scientific-sounding ruse against the people.
rows.anchor: göklerin yerin rabbi güya semâyı rasad etmekle görünmesi lâzım gelen bir cisim ve cismânî imiş gibi tevehhüm ettirerek halka karşı ilm ü fen yolundan bir desîse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means to fire clay in a kiln for making bricks; it does not explicitly say “bake bricks.”
rows.anchor: “tuğla pişir” demeyip bu tâbiri kullanması, kerpici pişirip tuğla yapmayı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported explanation says Pharaoh first conceived the craft of making fired bricks and thereby taught the technique.
rows.anchor: kerpici pişirip tuğla yapmayı ibtidâ Firavun düşünmüş olduğundan bu suretle sanatı tâlim eylemiş deniliyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ṣarḥ is a tall tower built as an observation post to survey the heavens.
rows.anchor: Hemen bana bir kule yap semâyı tarassud edecek bir rasad kulesi binâ et

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though he considers Moses a liar, Pharaoh pretends to conduct an empirical search to expose him and even to confront Moses’s God if found.
rows.anchor: her ihtimâle karşı güya ilm ü fen dairesinde bilfiil taharriyât yaparak o yalanı meydana çıkaracak ve şayet onun ilâhını bulursa güya onun da hakkından gelecek imiş gibi görünmek istiyor.

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some say Pharaoh’s statement remained empty talk and that trying to reach the sky with such a tower is irrational.
rows.anchor: Bazıları bunun sade bir laftan ibaret kaldığını ve öyle bir kule ile göğe çıkmaya çalışmanın gayr-i ma‘kūl olduğunu söylemişlerse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other accounts report that the tower was built and later collapsed.
rows.anchor: diğer taraftan böyle bir kulenin yapılıp yıkıldığını nakletmişlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iḥḍār means being seized and brought into the presence of God.
rows.anchor: İhzar edilenlerden “İhzâr” yakalanıp Hakk’ın huzûruna getirilmek.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disavowing leaders say they led their followers astray through their own desires, just as they themselves went astray, not by compulsion.
rows.anchor: Biz kendi hevâmızla azdığımız gibi onları da cebr ile değil, kendi hevâlarıyla azdırdık.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alleged partners say the followers were not really worshipping them; they were worshipping their own desires.
rows.anchor: Onlar Bize tapmıyorlardı kendi keyiflerine tapıyorlardı.
